Saadia-specific moves preserved per data-source/saadia-gloss-table.json; Blau's notes (data-source/blau-genesis-notes.json) consulted for Bereshit 1-12.

translations.1: Then Moses called together all the house of Israel, and said to them: 'You have witnessed all that God did in your presence in the land of Egypt — with Pharaoh, and with all his officers, and with the rest of the people of his land;
translations.2: the great signs which your eyes beheld, and those wonders and the great proofs —
translations.3: yet God has not given you a heart to know the like of them, nor do you see with your eyes, nor hear with your ears, unto this our day.
translations.4: And I led you forty years through the wilderness; your garments did not wear out upon you, and your sandals upon your feet;
translations.5: and the food which you were accustomed to — you did not eat it; and wine and strong drink you did not drink — so that He might say to you: so that you may know that I am God your Lord.
translations.6: Until you arrived at this place; and Sihon king of Heshbon and Og king of the Bashan came out to meet us for battle — and we slew them both.
translations.7: And we took their lands, then gave them as a possession to the Reubenites and the Gadites and half the tribe of Manasseh.
translations.8: So keep all the words of this covenant, and act by it, so that you may succeed in all that you do.'
translations.9: You are standing today, all of you, before God your Lord — your chiefs and your tribes, and your elders and your overseers, and the rest of the men of the house of Israel;
translations.10: your children and your women, and the stranger who is in the midst of your camp, from the hewer of your wood to the drawer of your water —
translations.11: to enter you into the covenant of God your Lord, and into His obligation, which He is making with you today;
translations.12: so that He may establish you today as a nation for Him, and He may be your God, as He promised you and as He swore to your fathers — to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob.
translations.13: And it is not with you alone that I am making this covenant and this obligation —
translations.14: but with whoever is present with us today, standing before God our Lord, and with whoever is not present with us today, since it is being transmitted to him.
translations.15: And you are well aware of what we dwelt through in the land of Egypt, and how we journeyed among the nations through whom you passed;
translations.16: and you have seen their abominations and their idols — of wood and stone, of silver and gold — which are with them.
translations.17: Lest there be found among you a man or a woman, or a clan or a tribe, whose heart is turning away today from God our Lord, to go and worship the objects of worship of those nations — lest there be among you a root bearing poisonous or bitter fruit.
translations.18: And if such a one hears the words of this obligation, he reckons within himself, saying: 'I shall have nothing but peace' — though he walks in the desire of his heart — so that he passes through in satiety while others thirst.
translations.19: God will not will to pardon him for that; rather, at that time God's anger and His wrath shall intensify against him, and all the obligation written in this book shall cling to him — until God blots out his name from beneath the sky.
translations.20: And God shall set him apart for evil, from among all the tribes of Israel, according to all the obligation of the covenant written in the book of this Torah.
translations.21: And the later generation — from your children who shall arise after you, and the stranger who comes from a distant land — when they look upon the plagues of that land and its diseases with which God afflicted it,
translations.22: all its soil being burned with fire and brimstone, so that it is not sown, and does not grow, and nothing of grass springs up from it — like the overthrow of Sodom and Gomorrah, Admah and Zeboiim, which God overturned in His anger and His wrath —
translations.23: then all the nations shall say: 'For what cause did God do thus to this land? What is the reason for the intensity of this great anger?'
translations.24: And they shall answer: 'It is because they forsook the covenant of God, the God of their fathers, which He made with them when He brought them out of the land of Egypt;
translations.25: and they went and worshipped other objects of worship and bowed down to them — objects of worship that they did not know, and that had not been appointed as a portion for them.'
translations.26: And God's anger intensified against that land, and He brought upon it all the curse written in this book.
translations.27: And He uprooted its inhabitants from their land, with anger and wrath and great indignation, and cast them into another land — as it is this day.
translations.28: And they shall take heed and say accordingly: 'The hidden things belong to God our Lord; but all the revealed things — which belong to us and to our children forever — are that we should do all the words of this Torah.'
